info.description:
Fluxa is a multi-currency digital asset platform built on Stellar. It provides
wallets, instant transfers, FX conversions, scheduled recurring payments,
batch disbursements, fiat on/off-ramps, and a developer-friendly webhook system.

All endpoints under `/v1` require a Bearer API key in the `Authorization` header.

## API key scopes

An API key can be limited to specific resources and actions. Scopes have the
form `<resource>:<action>`, where action is `read` or `write`:

| Resource | Scopes | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| wallets | `wallets:read`, `wallets:write` | `/v1/wallets` (create, trustlines, contract wallet changes) |
| transfers | `transfers:read`, `transfers:write` | `/v1/transfers`, `/v1/transactions`, `/v1/schedules`, `/v1/refunds` |
| batches | `batches:read`, `batches:write` | `/v1/transfers/batch` |
| webhooks | `webhooks:read`, `webhooks:write` | `/v1/webhooks` |
| reports | `reports:read`, `reports:write` | `/v1/usage` (`reports:write` is reserved for report generation) |

Other scopes: `keys:*`, `audit:read`, `fiat:*`, `fx:*`, `fees:read`,
`beneficiaries:*`, `compliance:*`. `<resource>:*` grants both actions on one
resource and `*` grants everything.

On scoped resource groups, `GET`/`HEAD` need the `read` scope and every other
method needs the `write` scope. A key without the required scope gets `403`
with the stable error code `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, and the denial is written to
the audit log as `api_key.scope_denied` (key id, required scope, method and
path only; never the key itself).

**Compatibility:** keys created without scopes (including every key that
existed before scopes were introduced) have an empty scope list and keep full
access. `transfers:read`/`transfers:write` continue to grant
`batches:read`/`batches:write`, so keys issued before the batches scope keep
working. A scoped key that holds `keys:write` can only create keys with scopes
it holds itself. Dashboard (JWT) sessions are governed by roles, not scopes.

Lists transfers held by compliance screening. A held transfer is
persisted with status `compliance_hold` and is deliberately not
enqueued for settlement until it is approved.

post.description:
Releases a held transfer. The transaction is reset to `pending` and
then re-enqueued for settlement — in that order, because the
settlement engine skips any transaction that is not `pending`.

Decisions are terminal: approving an already-decided review returns
`409 REVIEW_ALREADY_DECIDED`, which is what stops two reviewers from
releasing the same payment twice.

post.description:
Creates a deferred payment held by the Stellar network until one of its
claimants satisfies their predicate. The org's source wallet funds it,
unless `sponsor_account` names a Fluxa-custodied wallet, in which case
the creation is wrapped in BeginSponsoringFutureReserves /
EndSponsoringFutureReserves and the sponsor pays the 0.5 XLM entry
reserve.

The returned `balance_id` is derived from the create operation, so it is
available without a second Horizon round trip.

400.description:
Malformed request, unsupported asset, no claimants, a sponsor Fluxa
does not custody, or an invalid claim predicate.

get.description:
Returns the stored balance together with its live status from Horizon
and whether a claimant could claim right now. `on_chain` is absent when
Horizon no longer knows the balance, which is what an already-claimed
balance looks like.

post.description:
Claims on behalf of a claimant account Fluxa custodies, after checking
the claimant's predicate is satisfiable right now. A predicate that does
not hold is rejected with 400 `PREDICATE_NOT_SATISFIABLE` and no
transaction is submitted.

`claimant_account` may be omitted when the balance has exactly one
Fluxa-custodied claimant.

400.description:
The claimant's predicate is not currently satisfiable
(`PREDICATE_NOT_SATISFIABLE`), the account is not a claimant, or no
custodied claimant could be resolved.

409.description: The balance has already been claimed, revoked or expired.
